samples.summary: The new cross-step safety gate (`if: steps.resolve.outputs.pr_number != ''`) has no test
samples.evidence: The head-SHA binding that confines the App token's writes to the PR that produced the run used to be an early `return` inside the same script; after this diff it only protects the write step via the step-level `if: steps.resolve.outputs.pr_number != ''` (ci-report.yml:269). If that `if:` is dropped or the output name is renamed, the write step runs with `PR_NUMBER=''` → `prNumber = NaN` and the whole point of the validation is gone — and, as the test file's own header says, the symptom is only visible after merge. The new tests in scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs assert only (a) no non-builtin `require`, and (b) which token each script step uses; neither `readReportSteps()` (lines 235-268) nor either test reads a step's `if:` or any `steps.resolve.outputs.*` reference. This is exactly the class of invariant the rest of this file guards structurally (cf. "the filtered heavy jobs gate every step", line 110), so the omission is a real coverage gap, not a taste point.

samples.summary: The rewritten comment-body logic (unknown-vs-empty skipped, gating-file section, lane line) ships with no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the whole report body: a new `gatingFiles` section with the `and N more` cap (ci-report.yml:322-328), a new UNKNOWN branch keyed on `skipped === null` versus `skipped.length === 0` (329-343) — a distinction the comments call the point of the change — and the lane-filtering line (347-351). None of this is executed by any test. The two new tests only inspect step tokens and `require` specs; the body-building code is never extracted or run. The file already demonstrates the feasible technique: `globToRegExp` is extracted from the same YAML and executed with `new Function` (lines 157-166), and `readReportSteps()` already returns the dedented script text, so the render function could be exercised with synthetic env/artifacts. As shipped, e.g. inverting `skipped === null` to `!skipped?.length` would keep every test green while making the comment claim the happy case whenever the job-list read failed.

samples.summary: The builtins guard has no positive control: if script extraction truncates, the loop body never runs and the test passes vacuously
samples.evidence: `ci-report.yml`'s scripts today contain only `require('fs')`, so the inner `assert.ok` at lines 289-296 never evaluates a failing case and the test is a pure negative check. Its only protection against a broken extractor is `steps.length >= 2` (line 285) plus the falsiness of an empty string — which does not catch a script that is extracted *partially* (e.g. if the `/^ {12}/` continuation rule at line 256 stops early because of an inner block or a differently-indented line), in which case a later `require('@actions/github')` would be silently missed and the guard would pass on precisely the bug it exists for. Contrast the sibling test at lines 213-219, which deliberately asserts its corpus exercises both branches. A control — assert the extracted script contains a known last line of the block, or that the matcher rejects a synthetic `require('@actions/github')` string — would make the coverage real.
searchedFor: read ci-report.yml script blocks for indentation edge cases

samples.summary: Final assertion in "keeps its reads off the App token" can never fail independently (dead assertion)
samples.evidence: A step has exactly one `github-token:` value, so a step that is both a reader and a writer necessarily fails either the readers loop (lines 331-339, token must equal the ambient literal) or the writers loop (341-349, token must reference the App token) before control reaches line 351. The `readers.some((r) => writers.includes(r)) === false` assertion therefore holds unconditionally given the earlier loops pass, and reads as coverage of the "one client per step" rule while proving nothing beyond them.

samples.summary: No test enforces the claimed invariant that untrusted values reach the script through `env:` and never via `${{ }}` interpolation
samples.evidence: ci-report.yml:271-278 states values are passed through `env:` "so a value cannot splice itself into source text", and the write step depends on PR_NUMBER/SKIPPED/GATING_FILES/GATING_TOTAL/LABEL_DECISION being present. Nothing checks either half: no test asserts the script bodies contain no `${{ ... }}` expression, and no test asserts every `process.env.X` referenced in a script has a matching `env:` key on that step (a typo in one of the five names would silently degrade the comment to the wrong branch, with no red X anywhere because this workflow runs post-merge on `workflow_run`). `readReportSteps()` already parses the step bodies, so both checks are a few lines away.

Repo-wide greps for pr_number, steps.resolve, ci-report, head_sha, app-token (node_modules excluded) surface no other guard, and no .trusted/scripts/test/ mirror exists. verdict.reason: The comment-body logic in ci-report.yml's write step (gatingFiles section with the "and N more" cap at 322-328; the UNKNOWN branch keyed on `skipped === null` vs `skipped.length > 0` at 329-343; the lane line at 347-351) is executed by no test. The only tests referencing ci-report.yml live in scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs: the globToRegExp drift test, which extracts and runs ONLY the glob helper via `new Function` (161-166), plus two text-scanning tests that treat `step.script` as a string (matchAll for require specs at 288; includes for endpoint names at 325-326) and assert on step tokens. readReportSteps() has exactly two callers (284, 324), both text-only, so nothing reaches the render logic. Repo-wide greps (excluding node_modules) for the body's literals - "CI scope unknown", "Reduced CI", "Full CI", "Skipped:", "harness-verification", GATING_FILES/gating_files, lanesFiltered, "skipped === null" - hit only the workflow, docs, verify-self.mjs (which produces lanesFiltered), and .agent-review artifacts; never a test. I additionally checked every test file repo-wide (scripts/agent/**, scripts/agent/eval/**, packages/**, the .trusted mirror), confirmed no root test/tests dir exists, grepped for dynamic-execution techniques (new Function, vm., AsyncFunction) that could run YAML-embedded script, and read failure-summary.mjs plus its test in case the renderer had been extracted - it has not. A mutation such as replacing `skipped === null` with `!skipped?.length` would keep every test green while making the comment claim the happy case whenever the job-list read failed. That is a behavior change with no meaningful test, major under the test-adequacy rubric, and the repo itself demonstrates the feasible extraction technique two tests above.
